headline: Extinction is permanent—when species disappear, they're gone forever
universal_truth: What disappears is gone; prevention beats restoration; irreversibility demands caution
fun_facts: 99.9% of all species that ever existed are now extinct—extinction is the norm, not the exception
The last extinction of a species you could have pet: the baiji dolphin, declared extinct in 2007
We are currently in the sixth mass extinction event, with species disappearing 100-1000 times faster than normal
discussion_questions: What have you lost that can never be recovered?
How should we weigh irreversible decisions?
What in your life is at risk of disappearing permanently?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: The dodo. The passenger pigeon. The Tasmanian tiger. Once gone, gone forever. No amount of technology or money or regret can bring back what's extinct. Permanence changes everything about how we should think and act.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Extinction isn't just about animals—it's about irreversibility. Some losses can't be undone. How should permanence affect our decisions?
cliff.prompt: How should we handle irreversible decisions?

options.text: Irreversible decisions require more caution, more information, and more humility—once done, they cannot be undone, so the stakes are fundamentally higher
options.response: Yes. Reversible mistakes are learning opportunities. Irreversible mistakes are just losses. The level of certainty required should match the permanence of consequences.

options.text: All decisions should be made the same way—carefully
options.response: Careful is good, but irreversibility genuinely raises stakes...

q1.title: Gone Forever
q1.script: Extinction is permanent. Not 'very difficult to reverse'—impossible. This permanence is psychologically hard to grasp. We're used to fixing things. Some things can't be fixed, only prevented.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Gone Forever"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Cascade Effects
q2.script: Species don't exist alone—they're in webs of relationship. When one disappears, others are affected. Extinction cascades through ecosystems. The same applies to any system—removing key elements destabilizes the whole.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Personal Extinction
q3.script: Some personal losses are also permanent: burned relationships, missed opportunities, spoken words. Not everything can be undone. Recognizing what's irreversible helps you act appropriately before, not after.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: What disappears is gone. Prevention beats restoration. Irreversibility demands caution—act accordingly.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 213—welcome to August! Tomorrow, we'll explore what it takes to last. Until then, identify something irreplaceable worth protecting.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Irreversibility Check - What Can't Be Undone?
growTrack.activity: What decisions or situations in your life are irreversible? Relationships, career choices, words spoken? How does recognizing their permanence change how you approach them? Prevention is the only option when restoration is impossible.
